title: Mastercard Launches Quantum Advisory Practice with QIZ Security and Releases PQC Readiness Whitepaper - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Mastercard's Advisors and Transformation division launched a Quantum Advisory Practice with partner QIZ Security plus a PQC-transition whitepaper for financial institutions, anchored to a 2029–2030 planning horizon and harvest-now-decrypt-later risk; it also cited a hybrid fraud-protection pilot with Oxford Quantum Circuits.

themes.theme: PQC advisory as a service line

insights.claim: Mastercard (NYSE: MA), via its Advisors and Transformation division, launched a Quantum Advisory Practice and a whitepaper on post-quantum cryptography transition strategies for banks, acquirers, payment service providers and fintechs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Payments networks are monetizing PQC migration as consulting revenue, signaling PQC is becoming a budgeted line item for financial institutions.

insights.claim: Mastercard frames post-quantum migration around a 2029–2030 planning horizon aligned with G7 Cyber Expert Group and FS-ISAC guidance, while treating harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure of long-lived financial data as an immediate risk.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Regulatory-aligned timelines put PQC spending in the 2026–2030 window; vendors selling crypto discovery and migration tooling benefit.

insights.claim: QIZ Security joins Mastercard's quantum advisory practice to provide automated cryptographic asset discovery, data-longevity risk registers, phased remediation roadmaps, cryptographic agility guardrails, and board-level reporting.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryptographic inventory and agility tooling is the practical first step of PQC programs; small vendors like QIZ gain distribution via large partners.

insights.claim: Mastercard is running quantum R&D with Oxford Quantum Circuits, including a hybrid quantum-classical pilot focused on financial fraud protection.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Mastercard is hedging on both sides of quantum: defensive PQC and offensive use-case exploration.
